newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 40,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 40,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 40,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
One trader estimated a range of 25,000 and 40,000 tonnes although another took a more sceptical view and forecast a range of 25,000 to 30,000 tonnes.
The EU awarded 30,350 tonnes in its last tender on June 18.
Traders noted that cumulative exports in the 1996/97 tender series are still lagging behind last year's.
Last week's award brought cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 2.25 million tonnes, compared with 2.39 million at the equivalent stage last season.
"We are lagging by quite a lot and with the market the way it is at the moment I don't know if it's going to recover," said one trader.
"The series goes on until the end of July, so things could change but it's quite a long way behind."
The maximum restitution level was forecast at 42.889 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kilos of sugar based on the spot August Matif contract. Last week's restitution was 42.168 Ecus.
Licences are currently valid until the end of September as the EU does not normally permit validity to extend into the new campaign. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
